description: Fuse Base64 decode with downstream error-detection (CRC/checksum) in a single SIMD pass, borrowing from fused decode+ECC in communication receivers. Since many Base64 payloads are immediately checksummed (JWT, S/MIME), computing the checksum during decode eliminates a second pass over the data.
mathematical_formalization: Normally: cost = T_decode + T_CRC (two passes). Fused: each 48-byte decoded block feeds directly into CRC32 via VPCLMULQDQ before storing. Fused cost: T_decode + delta where delta << T_CRC because data is already in registers.
analogical_connections: Communication receivers: Viterbi decode + CRC check in single pipeline
Database: predicate pushdown during decompression scan
Image processing: fused debayer + white-balance in single shader pass
implementation_hypothesis: After multiply-add packing produces 48 bytes in ZMM, feed directly into CRC32 using VPCLMULQDQ. Maintain running CRC state across blocks. Adds ~2-3 instructions per 48-byte block.
experiment_seed: Implement fused decode+CRC32 vs separate decode then CRC32. Measure total cycles for 1MB input. Expected: fused saves ~40% of standalone CRC cost.
